newsitem.title: KENYA: FOREIGNERS BUY ON NAIROBI BOURSE DESPITE STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGNERS BUY ON NAIROBI BOURSE DESPITE STRIKE.

text.p: The Nairobi bourse edged up on Friday as foreign investors showed renewed interest despite a national strike called by reformists demanding constitutional change ahead of elections, bourse floor officals said.
The Nariobi Stock Exchange 20-share index edged up 2.7 points to close at 3423.87. Turnover was down slightly to 11.3 million shillings from 12.1, traded on 237,021 shares.
The strike called by reformist opposition leaders had scant success, with barely 1,000 activists turning up for a rally in Nairobi's Uhuru Park.
Although a few traders stayed away all the brokerage houses were represented on the bourse floor, brokers said.
"It (the strike) didn't have any great impact, even some shares have gone up," said a trader from a leading brokerage house.
No bonds were traded as investors adopted a wait and see policy after the instability caused last week by the IMF's cancellation of a key aid package last Friday and opposition calls for a strike.
"The bond market has been mostly foreigners who are offloading, but they have not been selling of late in the last few days," said a broker.
"There's a lot of interest in bonds although there's no supply," he added.
Foreign investors bought 2,860 shares in Limuru Tea Company at 850 from 845. 300 Sasini Tea and Coffee shares changed hands, still pegged at 80.00.
In the commercial and services sector Kenya Airways traded unchanged at 8 shillings, with 13,554 shares sold. Nation Printers and Publishers shed two shillings to close at 117 traded on 712 shares.
Foreigners snapped up 10,573 Kenya Commercial Bank shares at 98 from 95.50. Despite trading 11,750 shares National Bank of Kenya remained pegged at 16 shillings.
Dunlop Kenya and Firestone East Africa Portland Cement lead the revival of foreign interest in the industrial sector.
Dunlop Kenya traded 50,000 shares at 560 unchanged, while EA Portland traded 120,620 shares at 40 from 42.50.
